$21 million in 2015. $290 million in 2019. Same company, same channel.

That is Jeff Hurst, then Chief Operating Officer of Expedia, testifying under oath about what it cost to advertise Vrbo on Google. A 13x increase in four years, sworn to by the executive who signed the invoices.

Expedia kept paying. In travel, that is where the demand was and there was nowhere else to get it.

Sit with that for a second. If one of the largest advertisers on earth could not negotiate its way out of a 13x rise, a local business on four thousand a month is not going to out-bid the problem either.

The defence was never better bidding. It is owning a channel nobody else sets the price of — your list, your content, your reviews, your repeat customers. Paid is rented. Build something you own next to it.

Source: Hurst testimony, US v. Google, federal antitrust trial, 2023.
